name: Augmentir
product: An AI-native connected-worker platform for digital work instructions, skills, training and frontline support in manufacturing and service operations.
targetCustomer: Manufacturers and industrial service organizations with distributed frontline workforces
buyer: VP Manufacturing, COO, plant operations or learning and development leader
fundingDisplay: At least $7.5M publicly disclosed; a November 2025 round was undisclosed
traction: Augmentir expanded its Augie suite with manufacturing-specific AI agents in February 2026; deployment scale is not publicly audited.
notes: This is a human-in-the-loop industrial copilot and workflow layer, with integrations into ERP, CMMS, QMS and MES. No evidence was found that it directly commands PLCs or closes a machine-control loop; defensibility rests on workflow integration and accumulated frontline context rather than hardware.

name: MaintainX
product: A mobile-first maintenance and asset-management platform combining work orders, procedures, parts, analytics and sensor-agnostic machine-health monitoring.
targetCustomer: Industrial, facilities and field-service organizations maintaining physical assets
buyer: Maintenance and reliability leader, plant manager or COO
fundingDisplay: $254M total raised
traction: MaintainX reported 11,000 customer companies, 11 million managed assets and 27 million work orders completed annually in July 2025.
notes: The moat is maintenance workflow ownership plus asset and work-order data. Sensors add a physical sensing loop, but actions generally remain human work orders rather than autonomous machine actuation. Autodesk signed a definitive approximately $3.6B acquisition agreement in May 2026; the deal was still subject to closing conditions as of this review.

sources.label: MaintainX $150M Series D and operating metrics

name: Phaidra
product: Reinforcement-learning control agents that continuously optimize cooling, power and other mission-critical facility systems, with a current focus on AI data centers.
targetCustomer: Data-center operators and owners of complex industrial facilities
buyer: Data-center operations, facilities, energy or engineering leader
fundingDisplay: More than $110M announced; lower bound from $60M through Jul 2024 plus a greater-than-$50M Series B
traction: Phaidra has announced production and pilot control deployments with data-center operators including ST Telemedia GDC and Khazna; these are company or partner reported.
notes: Unlike monitoring software, Phaidra closes the physical loop through existing building and industrial control systems. It owns the control intelligence, not facility hardware. This creates high technical depth but also long integration, safety-validation and enterprise sales cycles.

name: Ethon
product: An industrial AI platform combining visual inspection, time-series analytics, causal root-cause analysis, process optimization and operator workflows across factory data sources.
targetCustomer: Large manufacturers operating multi-site production networks
buyer: VP Manufacturing, quality leader, process engineering or plant operations leader
fundingDisplay: CHF 15M Series A; USD equivalent not normalized
traction: The Series A announcement names Siemens Smart Infrastructure and Lindt & Spruengli as customers and describes a Siemens rollout to additional factories in Europe and the US.
notes: Ethon is broader than point visual inspection: it integrates historians, MES, IoT and unified-namespace data and can recommend or automatically adjust process setpoints where customers connect control systems. It does not sell new control hardware; the closed loop therefore depends on plant integration and customer governance.

name: Instrumental
product: A manufacturing data and AI platform that combines images, test and process data to detect defects, find root causes and manage production controls for electronics manufacturing.
targetCustomer: Electronics brands, product engineering teams and contract manufacturers
buyer: NPI, quality, manufacturing engineering or operations leader
fundingDisplay: More than $80M announced
traction: Instrumental reported tripled bookings and 150% net revenue retention in 2021; current public audited operating metrics were not found.
notes: This is more than a thin computer-vision SaaS product: it ingests existing AOI, X-ray, test and MES data, supports production-control workflows and can add drop-in inspection stations. It remains largely an engineering and quality decision layer rather than a general-purpose PLC actuator.

sources.label: Instrumental $50M Series C and total funding

name: Elementary
product: A no-code visual-inspection platform with edge devices, cameras and QualityOS software for automated manufacturing quality control.
targetCustomer: Discrete and process manufacturers automating visual quality inspection
buyer: Quality, manufacturing engineering or plant operations leader
fundingDisplay: At least $47.5M through Dec 2021; a 2024 strategic investment was undisclosed
latestRound: Strategic investment from Rockwell Automation, May 2024 (amount undisclosed)
traction: Elementary reported more than 250 million inspections at its December 2021 Series B; no current audited inspection count was found.
notes: This is the most productized point-CV profile in the set: real edge hardware and inspection data, but a narrower moat than broad factory orchestration. It closes the quality-inspection loop through pass/fail workflows and integrations, not a general machine-control loop.

name: Tractian
product: An integrated industrial operations system combining wireless condition-monitoring sensors, CMMS, OEE software and AI-assisted maintenance workflows.
targetCustomer: Industrial plants seeking to reduce downtime and digitize maintenance
buyer: Maintenance, reliability, plant operations or manufacturing leader
fundingDisplay: Approximately $200M total raised
traction: Tractian's Series C announcement describes deployments at manufacturers including Bosch, Embraer and Hyundai; customer counts and savings are company reported.
notes: The combination of owned sensors, condition data and maintenance workflows creates a stronger hardware-data moat than software-only CMMS vendors. It senses the physical loop continuously, but the public product remains human-in-the-loop for maintenance decisions and work execution rather than autonomous actuation.

name: Gecko Robotics
product: Wall-climbing and aerial inspection robots plus the Cantilever data platform for structural assessment and digital models of critical infrastructure.
targetCustomer: Defense, energy, oil and gas, power, steel, mining and heavy-industry asset owners
buyer: Asset integrity, inspection, maintenance or engineering leader
fundingDisplay: Approximately $347M; $125M Series D verified directly
traction: A 2026 US Navy IDIQ contract has a $71M ceiling, with an initial order valued up to $54M, for robotic inspection and data services.
notes: Gecko has a defensible robot, sensor and inspection-data stack with difficult field deployment and compliance knowledge. Its physical loop is autonomous sensing and inspection, not control of the inspected asset. The cumulative funding total is a credible-secondary estimate.

sources.label: Gecko history, headquarters and $125M Series D

name: GrayMatter Robotics
product: AI-driven robotic cells for autonomous scanning, sanding, grinding, polishing, buffing and spraying of high-mix manufactured parts.
targetCustomer: Manufacturers with labor-intensive surface-finishing operations
buyer: VP Manufacturing, plant manager, automation or operations leader
fundingDisplay: $70.4M total raised
traction: GrayMatter sells production systems across multiple surface-finishing processes; current audited deployment or revenue counts were not found.
notes: This is a direct closed physical loop: the system perceives each part and autonomously executes an application-specific finishing process. The moat is integrated perception, controls, process data and deployment expertise rather than a generic robot foundation model.

name: Bright Machines
product: Modular robotic assembly and inspection cells with software for line orchestration, traceability, analytics and design for automated assembly.
targetCustomer: Electronics, compute and industrial-equipment manufacturers
buyer: Manufacturing, automation, operations or supply-chain leader
fundingDisplay: More than $400M total capital, including disclosed venture debt
latestRound: $126M Series C, Jun 2024 ($106M equity plus $20M venture debt)
traction: Bright Machines reports more than 300,000 cumulative server units produced through its systems; the metric is company reported.
notes: Bright Machines directly closes assembly and inspection loops and is highly vertically integrated across cells, controls and software. That integration is a deployment moat but creates material hardware gross-margin, supply-chain and capital-intensity risk.

name: Standard Bots
product: Vertically integrated industrial robot arms, actuators and AI software intended to let factory workers teach tasks through demonstration rather than conventional robot programming.
targetCustomer: US manufacturers, including small and midsize factories
buyer: Manufacturing, automation, engineering or operations leader
fundingDisplay: At least $263M from $63M reported through 2024 plus a $200M Series C
traction: Standard Bots says its systems are deployed at hundreds of US companies; that count and its goal to supply 10% of new US industrial robots in 2027 are company reported.
notes: The company owns the robot, actuators, control stack and deployment experience, so this is a direct physical loop with a genuine hardware moat. However, demonstration-trained autonomy and deployment-scale claims are newer and less independently evidenced than those of established industrial-robot vendors.

name: Vention
product: A unified cloud platform and modular hardware ecosystem for designing, ordering, programming, deploying and operating industrial automation and robot cells.
targetCustomer: Small manufacturers through Fortune 500 factories deploying modular automation
buyer: Manufacturing engineering, automation, plant operations or COO
fundingDisplay: Approximately $263M total raised
traction: Vention reports 25,000 machines deployed across more than 4,000 factories and 25 manufacturing industries.
notes: Vention closes the physical loop through its controllers, edge hardware and robot applications while also owning the design-to-order workflow. Its modular catalog, installed base and reusable designs create an ecosystem moat; all deployment counts are company reported.

name: Physical Intelligence
product: Vision-language-action foundation models intended to transfer general manipulation skills across multiple robot embodiments and tasks.
targetCustomer: Robot manufacturers, robotics developers and enterprises deploying general-purpose manipulation
buyer: Robotics R&D, product or autonomy leader
fundingDisplay: At least $1.0B across reported 2024 and 2025 rounds; a reported 2026 raise in progress is excluded
traction: The company has released multiple robot-learning models and papers, but no public audited commercial deployment or revenue metric was found.
notes: This is software and research, not a robot-hardware company. Its moat thesis is model quality and heterogeneous real-world robot data; low vertical integration and limited public commercial evidence make transfer reliability, safety and monetization key risks.

name: Skild AI
product: The Skild Brain is a general-purpose robotics foundation model designed to control multiple robot forms and learn from simulation, internet video, teleoperation and real-world deployments.
targetCustomer: Robot OEMs and enterprises deploying robots across industrial and service environments
buyer: Robotics product, autonomy, innovation or operations leader
fundingDisplay: At least $1.7B from publicly announced Series A and C rounds; intervening financing is not normalized
traction: Skild reported live revenue rising from zero to approximately $30M within several months in 2025 and deployments in security, construction, delivery, data centers, warehouses and factory assembly; these figures are company reported.
notes: Skild combines frontier model research with an explicit cross-embodiment data flywheel. Its April 2026 acquisition of Zebra Technologies' robotics business, including Fetch Robotics assets, adds fleet, hardware and deployment integration, but public evidence does not yet establish broad task generalization independently.

name: FieldAI
product: On-edge risk-aware autonomy software that enables different robot types to navigate and act in dynamic industrial environments without prior maps, GPS or predefined routes.
targetCustomer: Construction, energy, mining, logistics, security and public-sector operators
buyer: Robotics, field operations, safety or innovation leader
fundingDisplay: $405M across two consecutive rounds
traction: FieldAI reported testing and deployments across hundreds of industrial environments in August 2025 and production deployments across three continents in 2026; both metrics are company reported.
notes: FieldAI directly closes navigation and task-level physical loops on third-party robots but does not own the core robot hardware. Its edge execution, risk modeling and multi-embodiment field data are the moat thesis; integration with customer robots and command workflows remains essential.

name: Figure
product: A full-stack humanoid robot platform combining proprietary robot hardware, the Helix vision-language-action model and in-house manufacturing.
targetCustomer: Manufacturers, logistics operators and eventually commercial and household users
buyer: Manufacturing, logistics, automation or innovation leader
fundingDisplay: More than $1B committed in Series C; cumulative total not normalized
traction: Figure and TIME reported Figure 02 robots working 10-hour shifts at a BMW plant in 2025; Figure signed a commercial deployment agreement with Catalyst Brands in May 2026. These are not audited fleet-scale metrics.
notes: Figure controls the entire physical loop—humanoid hardware, VLA model, data collection and BotQ manufacturing. That creates a potential hardware-data flywheel but also extreme capital intensity, safety and reliability risk; customer deployments remain early relative to the valuation and funding scale.

name: Dexterity
product: AI-powered industrial robot systems for truck loading, unloading, parcel handling, palletizing and other warehouse manipulation tasks.
targetCustomer: Parcel carriers, logistics operators, retailers and large warehouses
buyer: Warehouse automation, logistics operations or supply-chain leader
fundingDisplay: Approximately $291M total raised
traction: Public reports name FedEx, UPS, GXO and Sagawa among deployments or development customers; customer relationships are reported, while fleet and revenue scale are not audited publicly.
notes: Dexterity closes the physical loop with perception, force-aware manipulation and application software. It does not manufacture every arm—Kawasaki is a key hardware partner—but system integration, touch/force data and production logistics workflows provide a substantial deployment moat.

name: ANYbotics
product: The ANYmal autonomous quadruped robot performs repeatable visual, thermal, acoustic and gas inspections in hazardous industrial facilities.

fundingDisplay: More than $130M total raised
traction: ANYbotics cited large orders from BP, Equinor, Petrobras, Novelis and Outokumpu in December 2024; these order signals are company reported.

name: PhysicsX
product: An AI-native engineering platform using learned physics models to accelerate simulation, design optimization and operational digital twins for advanced industrial systems.
targetCustomer: Aerospace, automotive, semiconductor, energy, materials and industrial-machinery organizations
buyer: Engineering, R&D, simulation, product-development or manufacturing leader
fundingDisplay: At least $487M across publicly announced Series A-C rounds
traction: PhysicsX reported doubling recognized revenue, tripling booked revenue and more than doubling customer count year over year by June 2026; all figures are company reported and absolute revenue was not disclosed.

name: Neural Concept
product: A CAD-native, physics-aware enterprise AI platform for building design copilots, predicting product performance and optimizing engineering workflows.
targetCustomer: Automotive, aerospace, energy, semiconductor, electronics and defense engineering organizations
buyer: Engineering, simulation, R&D or product-development leader
fundingDisplay: At least $127M from publicly announced Series B and C rounds
traction: Neural Concept reported more than 50 enterprise customers and fourfold enterprise-revenue growth over 18 months in December 2025; these metrics are company reported.
notes: Neural Concept is an engineering copilot and learned-physics layer, not a physical-control or robot-hardware company. CAD/CAE integration and customer-specific geometry and simulation data are the moat thesis; incumbent engineering-software vendors remain a material platform risk.
